content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text weighs the challenger's chain against the defender's chain by their footing, which is exactly the chain-versus-chain collision this rule governs.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side", "room": "The judge's 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' read against the rule's 'states the contrary in its own words': reading one, a footing gap where the chain's supported steps never establish Joseph as begetter; reading two, the retired stating-verse test faulting the chain because no verse names Joseph in its own words; reading one controls because the judge calls both chains footed, weighs them symmetrically by their support, and ties them as UNDERDETERMINED rather than dismissing either.", "why": "The judge weighs both chains by footing, finds each footed with a structural gap or dependency, and lets the tie stand without deciding either chain by the absence of a verse stating its claim in its own words."}
